items.stem: State any three reasons for charging depreciation.
items.answer: Matching of costs and revenue; Consideration of tax; True and fair financial position; Compliance with law
items.markingKey: Any three of: Matching of costs and revenue; Consideration of tax; True and fair financial position; Compliance with law (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about depreciation is correct?
items.answer: Depreciation is charged on fixed assets, not on current assets.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Depreciation is charged on fixed assets, not on current assets.
options: Depreciation is a source of cash for the business.
Depreciation applies to natural resources as depletion and to stock as obsolescence.
Depreciation is charged on fixed assets, not on current assets.
Depreciation is charged on the market value of the asset each year.

items.stem: Explain the following causes of depreciation: (i) Expiry of legal rights (ii) Wear and tear due to use.
items.answer: (i) Expiry of legal rights: Assets such as patents or leases lose value as the right expires. (ii) Wear and tear due to use: Physical deterioration of the asset as it is used.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Assets such as patents or leases lose value as the right expires. (ii) Physical deterioration of the asset as it is used.

items.stem: A delivery van of Verma Retail has run 1,50,000 km and its engine and tyres are worn out. Which cause of depreciation is illustrated?
items.answer: Wear and tear due to use
items.markingKey: (b) Wear and tear due to use. Physical deterioration through use.
options: Expiry of legal rights
Wear and tear due to use
Obsolescence
Abnormal factors

items.stem: Mehta Stores took a shop on a 10-year lease; 7 years have now passed. Which cause of depreciation is illustrated? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Expiry of legal rights. The value of the lease falls as its term runs out.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Expiry of legal rights; 2 marks for the justification: The value of the lease falls as its term runs out.

items.stem:
Manish, owner of Thakur Retail, bought a delivery van for ₹6,00,000 three years ago. He has not charged any depreciation because "the van is still running well".
(i) What is the effect on the profit and the balance sheet? (ii) Give two reasons why depreciation must be charged.
items.answer: (i) Profit is overstated every year and the van is shown above its true value, so statements are not true and fair. (ii) Matching of cost with revenue; true financial position; tax deduction; compliance with law (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Profit is overstated every year and the van is shown above its true value, so statements are not true and fair. (ii) Matching of cost with revenue; true financial position; tax deduction; compliance with law (any two).

items.stem: Explain the following factors affecting the amount of depreciation: (i) Useful life (ii) Depreciable cost.
items.answer: (i) Useful life: Period over which the asset is expected to be used. (ii) Depreciable cost: Cost less estimated net residual value.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Period over which the asset is expected to be used. (ii) Cost less estimated net residual value.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the causes of depreciation?
items.answer: Depreciable cost
items.markingKey: (d) "Depreciable cost" is one of the factors affecting the amount of depreciation, not one of the causes of depreciation.
options: Expiry of legal rights
Wear and tear due to use
Obsolescence
Depreciable cost

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Useful life"?
items.answer: The period over which an asset is expected to be used by the enterprise.
items.markingKey: (b) Useful life: The period over which an asset is expected to be used by the enterprise.
options: The reduction in the quantity of a natural resource, such as a mine or quarry, as it is extracted.
The period over which an asset is expected to be used by the enterprise.
A decline in the value of a fixed asset due to use, passage of time or obsolescence; the systematic allocation of its depreciable cost over its useful life.
The estimated net amount an asset will fetch at the end of its useful life.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The estimated net amount an asset will fetch at the end of its useful life."
items.answer: Residual (scrap) value
items.markingKey: (d) Residual (scrap) value: The estimated net amount an asset will fetch at the end of its useful life.
options: Amortisation
Obsolescence
Depreciation
Residual (scrap) value

items.stem: The old printing machine of Thakur Industries still works but buyers now want digital prints that it cannot produce. Which cause of depreciation is illustrated?
items.answer: Obsolescence

options: Wear and tear due to use
Abnormal factors
Expiry of legal rights
Obsolescence

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the factors affecting the amount of depreciation?
items.answer: Depreciable cost

options: Depreciable cost
Abnormal factors

items.stem: Which method of depreciation has this feature: the amount of depreciation falls year after year?
items.answer: Written down value method
items.markingKey: (b) Written down value method: the amount of depreciation falls year after year.
options: Straight line method
Written down value method
Original cost method
Fixed instalment method

items.stem: Which of the following is true of straight line method but not of written down value method?
items.answer: Suitability: assets with small repairs and certain life, such as leases and patents

Recognition by income tax law: accepted by income tax authorities
Book value: never becomes zero
Suitability: assets with small repairs and certain life, such as leases and patents

Assertion (A): The straight line method is suitable for patents and leases.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true and R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.answer: ₹11,150 per year; rate 9.49%

items.stem: Bose Stores purchased machinery for ₹7,60,000 on 1 April 2023. Depreciation is charged at 25% per annum on the written down value method; accounts close on 31 March. Find the depreciation for each of the first 3 years and the book value at the end of year 3.
items.markingKey: Year-wise depreciation = 25% of opening book value: ₹1,90,000, ₹1,42,500, ₹1,06,875; book value = ₹7,60,000 − ₹4,39,375 = ₹3,20,625.

items.stem: A machine costing ₹5,22,000 was bought on 1 January 2024. Depreciation is 20% p.a. by the written down value method; the accounting year ends on 31 March. Find the depreciation for 2024-25 and 2025-26.
An asset costs ₹1,00,000. Compare the depreciation charged in the third year at 20% under the straight line method and the written down value method, and explain why they differ.
items.markingKey: SLM: 20% of original cost every year = ₹20,000 (1). WDV: book value at the start of year 3 = ₹64,000, depreciation ₹12,800 (1). WDV charges decline because the rate applies to a falling book value; SLM is constant (1).

items.stem: A machine costing ₹2,10,000 was bought on 1 October 2024. Depreciation is 10% p.a. by the straight line method; the accounting year ends on 31 March. Find the depreciation for 2024-25 and 2025-26.

Singh Retail bought a printing press for ₹2,85,000 and spent ₹6,500 on its transport and installation. Its useful life is 4 years and residual value ₹26,000. Calculate the annual depreciation by the straight line method.
items.markingKey: Depreciation = (cost + installation − residual value) ÷ life = (₹2,85,000 + ₹6,500 − ₹26,000) ÷ 4 = ₹66,375.

items.stem: Patel Brothers bought a printing press for ₹5,95,000 and spent ₹45,000 on its transport and installation. Its useful life is 4 years and residual value ₹6,000. Calculate the annual depreciation by the straight line method.
items.markingKey: Depreciation = (cost + installation − residual value) ÷ life = (₹5,95,000 + ₹45,000 − ₹6,000) ÷ 4 = ₹1,58,500.

items.stem: Chopra Traders bought a computer system for ₹55,000 and spent ₹1,000 on its transport and installation. Its useful life is 5 years and residual value ₹6,000. Calculate the annual depreciation by the straight line method.
items.markingKey: Depreciation = (cost + installation − residual value) ÷ life = (₹55,000 + ₹1,000 − ₹6,000) ÷ 5 = ₹10,000.

items.stem: Distinguish between straight line method and written down value method on the basis of annual depreciation, basis of charge, book value and recognition by income tax law.
items.answer: (i) Annual depreciation: straight line method: remains the same every year; written down value method: decreases every year. (ii) Basis of charge: straight line method: original cost; written down value method: book value at the beginning of each year. (iii) Book value: straight line method: can become zero at the end of the life; written down value method: never becomes zero. (iv) Recognition by income tax law: straight line method: not generally accepted for tax; written down value method: accepted by income tax authorities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Annual depreciation: straight line method: remains the same every year; written down value method: decreases every year. (ii) Basis of charge: straight line method: original cost; written down value method: book value at the beginning of each year. (iii) Book value: straight line method: can become zero at the end of the life; written down value method: never becomes zero. (iv) Recognition by income tax law: straight line method: not generally accepted for tax; written down value method: accepted by income tax authorities.

items.stem: Chopra and Sons bought a printing press for ₹1,15,000 and spent ₹4,000 on its transport and installation. Its useful life is 8 years and residual value ₹10,000. Calculate the annual depreciation by the straight line method.
items.markingKey: Depreciation = (cost + installation − residual value) ÷ life = (₹1,15,000 + ₹4,000 − ₹10,000) ÷ 8 = ₹13,625.

items.stem: An asset costs ₹2,50,000. Compare the depreciation charged in the third year at 10% under the straight line method and the written down value method, and explain why they differ.

(iii) Suitability: straight line method: assets with small repairs and certain life, such as leases and patents; written down value method: assets needing more repairs as they age, such as plant and machinery.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Basis of charge: straight line method: original cost; written down value method: book value at the beginning of each year. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Asset disposal account"?
items.answer: An account opened on sale of an asset, to which the cost, accumulated depreciation and sale proceeds are transferred to find the profit or loss.
items.markingKey: (c) Asset disposal account: An account opened on sale of an asset, to which the cost, accumulated depreciation and sale proceeds are transferred to find the profit or loss.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Reserve"?
items.answer: An amount set aside out of profits to strengthen the financial position or for future needs; an appropriation of profit.

A revenue reserve not created for any specific purpose, to strengthen the business.

items.answer: (i) (a) Provision (charge against profit, ₹20,000) (b) Revenue (general) reserve (appropriation) (c) Capital reserve. (ii) Only (a), the provision of ₹20,000; reserves are appropriations made out of profit.

items.stem:
The directors of Menon Traders want to show lower profits by charging depreciation at 40% on machinery whose real fall in value is about 15%, to avoid demands for higher dividends.

items.answer: (i) A secret reserve (assets are undervalued). (ii) For: it strengthens the business and follows prudence. Against: it violates full disclosure; statements no longer show a true and fair view and shareholders are misled.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) A secret reserve (assets are undervalued). (ii) For: it strengthens the business and follows prudence. Against: it violates full disclosure; statements no longer show a true and fair view and shareholders are misled.

items.stem: Distinguish between provision and reserve on any six bases.
items.answer: (i) Dividend: provision: cannot be used for dividends; reserve: revenue reserves can be used for dividends. (v) Presentation: provision: deducted from the asset or shown as a liability; reserve: shown under reserves and surplus. (vi) Effect on profit: provision: reduces net profit; reserve: does not reduce net profit; divisible profit is reduced.

items.stem: State one difference between straight line method and written down value method on the basis of basis of charge.
items.answer: straight line method: original cost; written down value method: book value at the beginning of each year
items.markingKey: 1 mark: straight line method: original cost; written down value method: book value at the beginning of each year

items.stem: Kulkarni Stores bought a machine for ₹3,10,000 on 1 April 2022 and charged depreciation at 10% p.a. by the straight line method (year ends 31 March). The machine was sold on 31 March 2024 for ₹2,87,000. Find the book value on the date of sale and the profit or loss on sale.
items.answer: Book value ₹2,48,000; profit ₹39,000

items.stem: What is meant by "General reserve"?
items.answer: A revenue reserve not created for any specific purpose, to strengthen the business.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A revenue reserve not created for any specific purpose, to strengthen the business.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Depreciation is charged on land.
Reason (R): Land generally has an unlimited useful life.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: land is not depreciated. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Kulkarni Traders bought a printing press for ₹2,30,000 and spent ₹17,500 on its transport and installation. Its useful life is 4 years and residual value ₹13,000. Calculate the annual depreciation by the straight line method.
items.markingKey: Depreciation = (cost + installation − residual value) ÷ life = (₹2,30,000 + ₹17,500 − ₹13,000) ÷ 4 = ₹58,625.

items.stem: What is meant by "Book value"?
items.answer: Cost of an asset less the depreciation charged on it till date.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Cost of an asset less the depreciation charged on it till date.

items.stem: An asset costs ₹2,30,000. Compare the depreciation charged in the third year at 10% under the straight line method and the written down value method, and explain why they differ.
items.markingKey: SLM: 10% of original cost every year = ₹23,000 (1). WDV: book value at the start of year 3 = ₹1,86,300, depreciation ₹18,630 (1). WDV charges decline because the rate applies to a falling book value; SLM is constant (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors affecting the amount of depreciation?
items.answer: Wear and tear due to use
items.markingKey: (c) "Wear and tear due to use" is one of the causes of depreciation, not one of the factors affecting the amount of depreciation.
options: Useful life
Depreciable cost
Wear and tear due to use
Estimated net residual value

items.stem: Identify the item as a provision or a type of reserve. In each case give a reason. (i) Joshi Enterprises charges an amount against profit for taxes payable for the year. (ii) Joshi Enterprises sets aside profit to keep its dividend rate steady over years.
items.answer: (i) Provision: It provides for a known liability of uncertain amount. (ii) Specific reserve: Dividend equalisation is a specific purpose.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Provision (ii) Specific reserve

items.stem: Gupta Stores bought a machine for ₹2,90,000 on 1 April 2022 and charged depreciation at 20% p.a. by the written down value method (year ends 31 March). The machine was sold on 31 March 2024 for ₹2,02,100. Find the book value on the date of sale and the profit or loss on sale.
items.answer: Book value ₹1,85,600; profit ₹16,500

items.stem: A air-conditioning plant costing ₹1,73,000 (including installation) has a residual value of ₹16,000 after 10 years. Find the annual depreciation and the rate of depreciation on original cost under the straight line method.
items.answer: ₹15,700 per year; rate 9.08%

items.stem: The old printing machine of Singh Agencies still works but buyers now want digital prints that it cannot produce. Which cause of depreciation is illustrated? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Obsolescence. New technology has made the asset outdated.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Obsolescence; 2 marks for the justification: New technology has made the asset outdated.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about provisions and reserves is correct?
items.answer: General reserve is a revenue reserve.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: General reserve is a revenue reserve.
options: A provision is created only when there is profit.
A secret reserve is always disclosed in the notes.
Capital reserve is created out of normal trading profits.
General reserve is a revenue reserve.

items.stem: Thakur Industries purchased machinery for ₹7,40,000 on 1 April 2023. Depreciation is charged at 20% per annum on the written down value method; accounts close on 31 March. Find the depreciation for each of the first 3 years and the book value at the end of year 3.
items.markingKey: Year-wise depreciation = 20% of opening book value: ₹1,48,000, ₹1,18,400, ₹94,720; book value = ₹7,40,000 − ₹3,61,120 = ₹3,78,880.

items.stem: A machine costing ₹1,30,000, on which accumulated depreciation of ₹52,000 stands in the provision for depreciation account, is sold by Joshi Enterprises for ₹74,000 by cheque. Pass the journal entries using an asset disposal account.
items.answer: (1) Asset Disposal A/c Dr ₹1,30,000; To Machinery A/c ₹1,30,000. (2) Provision for Depreciation A/c Dr ₹52,000; To Asset Disposal A/c ₹52,000. (3) Bank A/c Dr ₹74,000; To Asset Disposal A/c ₹74,000. (4) Profit and Loss A/c Dr ₹4,000; To Asset Disposal A/c ₹4,000.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: (1) Asset Disposal A/c Dr ₹1,30,000; To Machinery A/c ₹1,30,000. (2) Provision for Depreciation A/c Dr ₹52,000; To Asset Disposal A/c ₹52,000. (3) Bank A/c Dr ₹74,000; To Asset Disposal A/c ₹74,000. (4) Profit and Loss A/c Dr ₹4,000; To Asset Disposal A/c ₹4,000. Book value ₹78,000; loss ₹4,000.

items.stem: State one difference between straight line method and written down value method on the basis of recognition by income tax law.
items.answer: straight line method: not generally accepted for tax; written down value method: accepted by income tax authorities
items.markingKey: 1 mark: straight line method: not generally accepted for tax; written down value method: accepted by income tax authorities

items.stem: What is meant by "Specific reserve"?
items.answer: A reserve created for a particular purpose, such as a dividend equalisation reserve or debenture redemption reserve.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A reserve created for a particular purpose, such as a dividend equalisation reserve or debenture redemption reserve.

items.stem: Sethi Stores bought a printing press for ₹3,30,000 and spent ₹21,000 on its transport and installation. Its useful life is 4 years and residual value ₹5,000. Calculate the annual depreciation by the straight line method.
items.markingKey: Depreciation = (cost + installation − residual value) ÷ life = (₹3,30,000 + ₹21,000 − ₹5,000) ÷ 4 = ₹86,500.

items.stem: What is meant by "Asset disposal account"?
items.answer: An account opened on sale of an asset, to which the cost, accumulated depreciation and sale proceeds are transferred to find the profit or loss.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: An account opened on sale of an asset, to which the cost, accumulated depreciation and sale proceeds are transferred to find the profit or loss.

items.stem: An asset costs ₹3,50,000. Compare the depreciation charged in the third year at 10% under the straight line method and the written down value method, and explain why they differ.
items.markingKey: SLM: 10% of original cost every year = ₹35,000 (1). WDV: book value at the start of year 3 = ₹2,83,500, depreciation ₹28,350 (1). WDV charges decline because the rate applies to a falling book value; SLM is constant (1).

items.answer: Expiry of legal rights

items.stem: Identify the item as a provision or a type of reserve. In each case give a reason. (i) Patel Agencies sets aside profit to keep its dividend rate steady over years. (ii) Patel Agencies charges an amount against profit for taxes payable for the year.
items.answer: (i) Specific reserve: Dividend equalisation is a specific purpose. (ii) Provision: It provides for a known liability of uncertain amount.

items.stem: Goyal Agencies bought a machine for ₹1,10,000 on 1 April 2022 and charged depreciation at 20% p.a. by the straight line method (year ends 31 March). The machine was sold on 31 March 2024 for ₹69,500. Find the book value on the date of sale and the profit or loss on sale.
items.answer: Book value ₹66,000; profit ₹3,500
items.markingKey: Total depreciation for 2 years ₹44,000; book value ₹1,10,000 − ₹44,000 = ₹66,000 (2). Sale ₹69,500 − ₹66,000 = profit of ₹3,500 (1).
